description: AI image generation prompts for all 19 Pearson Gray-Scott pattern types. Validated for use with Midjourney, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion, Flux, and Gemini.
usage_note: Combine the 'base_prompt' with modifiers from 'color_prompts' and 'style_variations' to build complete prompts. Append 'negative_prompt' terms for Stable Diffusion workflows.
global_negative_prompt: blurry, low quality, cartoon, anime, text, watermark, oversaturated, 3D render, border, frame, gradient background, human figure

types.name: Uniform Red
types.base_prompt: flat monochromatic dark red field, zero texture, chemical equilibrium surface, featureless abstract
types.expanded_prompt: A perfectly uniform deep crimson surface with no spatial structure, like an overexposed photographic plate or annealed metal at rest. Zero pattern. Monochrome. Completely flat.

style_variations.artistic: minimalist abstract art, deep red void

types.negative_prompt: texture, pattern, spots, stripes, variation, noise

types.name: Uniform Blue
types.base_prompt: flat uniform deep blue field, zero texture, calm chemical equilibrium, featureless azure surface
types.expanded_prompt: A perfectly still, deep blue surface with absolutely no pattern or variation. Evokes a calm, windless ocean from directly above, or a clear sky at noon. No texture.

style_variations.artistic: minimalist calm abstract, deep blue void

types.negative_prompt: texture, pattern, spots, stripes, variation, noise, waves

types.name: Wavelet Chaos
types.base_prompt: turbulent chemical wave interference, chaotic overlapping spiral wavelets, constantly shifting reaction-diffusion chaos
types.expanded_prompt: A turbulent field of short-lived chemical wave packets that constantly form, collide, and dissolve. Like a disturbed water surface viewed from above, with overlapping circular waves creating interference patterns. Always moving, never settling. Spatiotemporal chaos.

types.expanded_prompt: A luminous blue ocean field swept by slow, large-scale traveling chemical waves. Dark voids — roughly circular dead zones — drift through the glowing wave field like holes in fabric. Viewed from directly above. Like bioluminescent plankton blooms with dead patches.

types.expanded_prompt: Sinuous organic stripes that look like fingerprint ridges or wood grain, but constantly rearranging. The stripes align locally in small domains, but grain boundaries between domains continuously shift and heal. Like a fingerprint that can never quite decide on its final pattern.

types.name: Turing Spots
types.base_prompt: hexagonal array of dark spots on light cream background, Turing pattern, cheetah-like spot organization, natural biological patterning
types.expanded_prompt: A near-perfect hexagonal lattice of dark circular spots on a light background. The spots are uniformly sized and spaced, arranged in the characteristic honeycomb geometry of close-packing. Looks exactly like cheetah fur or leopard skin spots. These are 'negative' spots — dark holes in a bright field.

types.name: Chaotic Mitosis
types.base_prompt: chaotic dividing cell pattern, blobs undergoing mitosis, amoeba colony splitting chaos
types.expanded_prompt: A dynamic field of cellular blobs in continuous mitotic division. Each blob grows, elongates along an axis, pinches in the middle, and splits into two daughter cells that immediately begin growing again. Chaotic because division direction and timing are unpredictable. Looks exactly like time-lapse cell division.

The channel walls are thick with a narrow void corridor inside. Like a hedge maze seen from a helicopter, or a river delta from satellite.

types.name: Mitotic Hexagons
types.base_prompt: perfect hexagonal spot lattice, honeycomb-organized circular dots, crystalline self-organized spot array
types.expanded_prompt: Circular spots arranged in a near-perfect hexagonal lattice — the most ordered packing of circles possible. Unlike type delta which has negative spots (holes), these are positive spots (raised islands) on a dark background. The arrangement emerged through self-organized mitosis. Like a crystallized soap bubble raft or a hexagonal-packed protein array.

Corduroy fabric, parallel muscle fibers, or one-direction zebra stripes.

types.expanded_prompt: Large sustained spiral waves emanating from multiple rotating organizing centers. The arms rotate continuously and can span much of the field. Multiple spiral cores compete for space. Identical in character to the famous Belousov-Zhabotinsky oscillating chemical reaction. Also resembles a galaxy viewed edge-on, or a slow-motion hurricane.

types.name: U-Skate World
types.base_prompt: self-propelled autonomous chemical structures moving through field, reaction-diffusion gliders, computational complexity pattern
types.expanded_prompt: Small autonomous structures that move through the chemical field like living organisms. Each unit is self-propelled and maintains its form while traveling. The field is an ecology of these entities — some collide and annihilate, others spawn new ones. The most computationally complex reaction-diffusion pattern. Like Game of Life gliders in a continuous chemical medium.

types.name: Red Soap Bubbles
types.base_prompt: soap bubble foam closed-cell structure, warm-toned cellular foam, Voronoi cell pattern with surface tension borders
types.expanded_prompt: Roughly circular closed cells bordered by a network of thin stripes. The interior of each cell is a distinct chemical state from the exterior. The topology is foam-like — cells pack together like soap bubbles, with three-way junctions where borders meet. The overall impression is surface tension in a warm, reddish field.
